artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan adopting Option A + C (shared corroboration function in skill-base.sh, wired into the handoff-present branch of all three orchestration engines) plus a re-scoped Option B (base-mode agent handoff contract, validate-handoff.sh as a log-only diagnostic), with paired prose-invariant edits and a scratch-deploy-tree verification gate.

memory_candidates.content: When a verification gate reads evidence from two independent sources (e.g. an orchestrator handoff and a plan file), an asymmetry can emerge where the WEAKER evidence path is handled and the STRONGER one is not: corroboration logic gated on a recovery-only signal becomes unreachable whenever the primary artifact exists but is merely incomplete. The structural fix is to make the corroboration trigger match the CONSUMER gate's own precondition exactly (here: phases_total == 0, the gate's Case-3 condition) rather than reusing the producer-side recovery signature (both counts zero), so trigger and consumer cannot drift. The safety argument then becomes structural rather than a promise: the always-refuse case is unreachable from the new trigger by construction, since it requires the opposite precondition. Related: extending such a trigger usually falsifies a stated prose invariant elsewhere in the same file (a 'MUST NOT' or read-allowlist scoping the read to one branch), so the prose edit must land in the SAME commit as the code, not as follow-up cleanup.
